core_problem_solved: To provide powerful and convenient high-level data binding (object mapping) functionality for processing JSON in Java, allowing for seamless conversion between Java Objects (POJOs) and their JSON string representations.
key_features: Automatic serialization (Java objects to JSON) and deserialization (JSON to Java objects)
Support for complex object graphs, generics, and polymorphism
A highly customizable mapping process through a rich set of annotations (from `jackson-annotations`)
A tree model (`JsonNode`) for manual JSON traversal and manipulation
era_and_niche: The modern, de facto industry standard for JSON processing in the Java ecosystem. It is the main, high-level library developers interact with and is the default library used in major frameworks like Spring Boot.
reason_for_obsolescence: This library is **not obsolete** and is actively maintained. It is the leading library in its category, sitting on top of `jackson-core` and `jackson-annotations`. Its primary competitor is Google's **`com.google.code.gson:gson`**, though Jackson is generally considered more feature-rich and is more widely used in enterprise frameworks.
